jsch generate --schema schema.json --out ./model --package model --type Catalog

exec go test -count=1 ./model

-- schema.json --
{
  "type": "object",
  "$defs": {
    "widget": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "sku":   {"type": "string"},
        "label": {"type": "string"}
      },
      "required": ["sku"]
    }
  },
  "properties": {
    "featured": {"$ref": "#/$defs/widget"}
  },
  "required": ["featured"]
}
-- go.mod --
module example.com/catalogpkg

go 1.27
-- model/model_test.go --
package model_test

import (
	"encoding/json/v2"
	"testing"

	model "example.com/catalogpkg/model"
)

// A camelCase / lowercase $defs key must still produce an exported Go
// type so callers in other packages can name and construct it. This
// test lives in an external _test package precisely to prove the type
// is reachable across the package boundary.
func TestWidget_ExportedAndConstructible(t *testing.T) {
	c := model.Catalog{
		Featured: model.Widget{Sku: "abc"},
	}
	out, err := json.Marshal(c)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Marshal: %v", err)
	}
	if string(out) != `{"featured":{"sku":"abc"}}` {
		t.Errorf("Marshal = %s", out)
	}
}
